plan.description: Strongest cloud model on every placement unit: gpt-5.5-cloud

Keep the strongest model on planning, implementation, and branch-control review, while moving non-user-facing test generation to the cheaper mini cloud model to explore cost/latency savings with limited expected quality risk.

rationale.understand_and_plan: Baseline used gpt-5.5-cloud and achieved 0.82 plus accuracy with no base failures; planning is upstream of all later work, so retain the strongest endpoint to preserve task understanding quality.
rationale.implement_solution: This is the final user-facing code-producing unit and likely the most quality-sensitive placement; keep gpt-5.5-cloud to avoid degrading solution correctness.
rationale.generate_tests: Test generation is non-user-facing, has no tool/structured-output requirement, and was one of the more expensive baseline units. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud has sufficient context and supports required capabilities while offering much lower token cost, making it a targeted cost-reduction experiment.
rationale.review_solution: Review controls conditional routing, so retain gpt-5.5-cloud to preserve reliable finish/revise decisions after tests.

plan.description: Evaluate the next major cost-reduction frontier by downgrading the final implementation step to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud while keeping all other non-user-facing stages on the cheaper mini cloud model except restoring planning to gpt-5.5-cloud to protect task understanding after candidate-3 showed base-pass degradation when planning was downgraded.

rationale.understand_and_plan: Candidate-3 moved planning to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud and reduced cost, but base_pass dropped from 1.0 to 0.94 with several base failures and latency worsened due to extra revision loops. Restore gpt-5.5-cloud for upstream task understanding to preserve the perfect base-pass behavior seen in baseline, candidate-1, and candidate-2.
rationale.implement_solution: This user-facing code-producing unit is the largest untested downgrade. Prior candidates kept gpt-5.5-cloud for implementation, so moving only this remaining quality-critical stage to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud explores whether the much cheaper model can maintain acceptable correctness when supported by strong planning plus mini-generated tests and review. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud has ample context and requires no tools or structured output for this unit.
rationale.generate_tests: Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because candidate-1 and candidate-2 showed this downgrade reduced test-generation cost from roughly 0.48 to about 0.02 while preserving or slightly improving aggregate plus accuracy versus baseline.
rationale.review_solution: Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because candidate-2 matched candidate-1 plus_pass at 0.84 while cutting review cost from about 0.43 to about 0.017 and lowering mean latency. It supports the needed branch-control context/capabilities, and no structured output is required.

plan.description: Probe whether the branch-control review step can be moved to the zero-cost local model while reverting test generation to the faster/safer mini cloud setup from candidate-4. This keeps the strongest observed planning choice and the best-performing mini-cloud implementation assignment, aiming to reduce cloud cost beyond candidate-4 without repeating candidate-5's slow local-test bottleneck.

rationale.understand_and_plan: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud for upstream task understanding: every evaluated placement with strong planning except candidate-5 maintained or nearly maintained perfect base pass, while candidate-3's mini planning caused base_pass to fall to 0.94 and increased revision loops/latency. Strong planning also underpinned the best observed aggregate quality in candidate-4 (plus_pass 0.86).
rationale.implement_solution: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for final user-facing implementation because candidate-4 demonstrated the best observed accuracy (plus_pass 0.86, base_pass 1.0) with mini implementation, while sharply reducing implementation cost versus gpt-5.5. The endpoint has ample context and no tool/structured-output requirement applies.
rationale.generate_tests: Restore gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for test generation rather than qwen-local. Candidate-5's local tests lowered test cloud cost to zero but caused high latency (mean 22.53s, p95 59.76s, 67 local test calls taking ~614s) and slightly worse quality than candidate-4. Mini-cloud tests were still extremely cheap (~0.021 in candidate-4), faster, and paired with the best observed quality.
rationale.review_solution: Move only review to qwen-local to isolate a local downgrade on the branch-control stage. Mini review is already cheap, but this explores zero-cloud-cost routing while avoiding the much larger latency penalty seen from local test generation. qwen-local supports tool calling, the workflow does not require structured output for review, and its 32k context window should be sufficient for test-result review decisions.

plan.description: Evaluate an all-mini-cloud placement to isolate whether the strong gpt-5.5 planner is still necessary now that candidate-4 showed gpt-4.1-mini can successfully handle implementation, tests, and review. This explores a much lower-cost fully cloud-based configuration without using the slower or lower-quality local model.

rationale.understand_and_plan: Prior mini planning in candidate-3 caused base_pass to drop to 0.94 when paired with gpt-5.5 implementation and extra loops, but that configuration differed from candidate-4's surprisingly strong all-mini downstream stack. Testing mini planning with mini implementation/tests/review completes the cloud-mini frontier and targets the dominant remaining cost in candidate-4 (~0.68 from gpt-5.5 planning) while preserving large context and endpoint capability.
rationale.implement_solution: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because candidate-4 demonstrated the best observed aggregate quality (plus_pass 0.86, base_pass 1.0) with mini implementation when supported by strong planning, while local implementation in candidate-7 degraded quality to 0.78 plus_pass and 0.92 base_pass. Mini is the safer inexpensive implementation choice.
rationale.generate_tests: Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for test generation: candidates 1, 2, and 4 showed mini tests are extremely cheap (~0.02 cloud cost), faster than local tests, and compatible with the best observed quality, whereas local tests in candidate-5 greatly increased latency and reduced base/plus performance.
rationale.review_solution: Keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for branch-control review because candidate-2 preserved quality while cutting review cost sharply, candidate-4 achieved the best observed quality with mini review, and candidate-6 showed local review reduced plus_pass to 0.82. gpt-4.1-mini supports the required context/capabilities and no structured output is required.
